reasoning: Multiple authoritative scientific organizations, including NOAA, Copernicus, the European Environment Agency (EEA), and the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC), confirm that Arctic sea ice has declined significantly since continuous satellite observations began in 1979. According to NOAA, the amount of summer sea ice has decreased at a rate of approximately 13% per decade. Furthermore, observations show that the Arctic is losing older, thicker multi-year ice, leaving behind younger and thinner first-year ice that is more vulnerable to melting.
